raw_market_forces.raw_market_force_name: Persistent High Interest Rates and Tight Financing Conditions
raw_market_forces.raw_description: High interest rates have persisted globally, impacting the cost of capital and dealmaking across industries, including mining. This environment has made acquirers more selective, favoring deals with clear, near-term value creation and synergies. The elevated cost of debt has particularly influenced capital-intensive sectors like mining, where large-scale investments and M&A require significant financing. The report notes that while interest rates came down slightly, they remained high enough to suppress a full revival in M&A activity, pushing companies to focus on scale deals and operational efficiencies.

raw_findings.content: Interest rates did come down just enough to reignite interest by private equity and other financial investors as that class began to regain ground with a 29% increase in deal value year over year. Corporate M&A, which is less influenced by small movements in the cost of debt, is on track to end the year 12% above 2023, with steady growth across all regions.

raw_examples.content: Scale deals accounted for 59% of the largest strategic deals in 2024—that’s the highest proportion since 2015. The popularity of scale deals was most prominent in industries with higher fixed costs—such as energy and natural resources.

relevant_facts.content: High interest rates have made acquirers more selective and have shifted focus toward deals with immediate, bankable synergies.

relevant_statistics.content: Corporate deals rose by 12% in value, while financial acquisitions rose by 29%. Scale deals accounted for 59% of the largest strategic deals in 2024.

relevant_quotes.content: Strategic acquirers were more selective in their deals, required more concrete value creation, were less willing to pay for long-term top-line growth, and, most dramatically, adjusted to the new M&A value equation by pursuing both revenue and cost synergies in tandem.

possible_structural_shifts: Preference for deals with immediate synergies
implications_on_future_of_sector: Mining companies may prioritize consolidation and operational efficiency over expansion.
